run_metadata.coverage_summary: Tier 1 Commonwealth (AusTender) swept via search and yielded the two genuinely-new, currently-open opportunities added this run (NIAA Indigenous Business Verification RFT and DFAT Climate Resilient Communities mid-term review). All nine core state/territory portals (NSW buy.nsw, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/supply.qld, Tenders WA, SA Tenders & Contracts, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL, ACT Tenders) were checked for recent activity; their fresh items surfaced this week were already captured in prior runs. Tier 2 (universities incl. University of Adelaide/UTS, GBEs incl. Sydney Water/Melbourne Water/Transgrid/ARTC/Inland Rail, CSIRO, NSW/QLD health) and Tier 3 (SAP Ariba Discovery, EstimateOne, VendorPanel, major-buyer corporate portals, WSA Co, Ramsay/Healthscope) were sampled. One new source (Healthscope) added.
gaps: WebFetch egress is blocked by the network egress proxy for every external tender domain tested this run (www.tenders.gov.au, www.vendorpanel.com.au, and a control host all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED / 403). All opportunity detail below is therefore reconstructed from WebSearch result snippets, not from a direct read of the tender detail page or its documents; tender documents, evaluation criteria weightings, and estimated values could not be extracted.

Tier 1 state/territory listing pages (NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, NT, ACT) could not be paginated directly (egress block + several require a logged-in session or email token); coverage of those jurisdictions this run relied on search snippets and known-item de-duplication rather than an exhaustive live sweep.

Tier 3 corporate e-sourcing hubs (SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network Discovery, Coupa, Jaggaer) and major-buyer portals (BHP, Woolworths, Coles, Qantas, WSA Co, Ramsay, Healthscope) are login/registration-gated and no authenticated session is available, so no individual corporate opportunity was visible; portals recorded in discovered_sources only. No corporate tender was fabricated.
Management-consultancy and panel/prequalified RFx (invitation-only) remain out of scope and were not fabricated.

DFAT Climate Resilient Communities mid-term review: the AusTender ATM ID was not verifiable from search snippets (a mirror aggregator reported an unconfirmed 'DFAT-1111'), so tender_id is left blank and a normalised dedup_key is used.

Candidate leads that proved stale/closed on inspection were excluded to avoid fabrication: Transgrid 'Sydney 40MW demand management' (that tender closed 31-Jul-2018) and CSIRO EOI CSIROEOI2026008 (CDSCC Canteen Services, closed 09-Jun-2026).
recommended_seed_additions: Healthscope — Suppliers / Procurement (private hospital group; corporate-website + procurement-contact sourcing, opportunities largely invitation/contact-based rather than a public tender board)

tenders.title: Indigenous business verification and associated services to support the Indigenous Procurement Policy
tenders.category: Business verification / registration and certification services
tenders.description: NIAA is approaching the market for a national, independent Indigenous business verification service and related functions to support implementation of the reformed (strengthened) Indigenous Procurement Policy (IPP). The provider will give the Commonwealth and the public trusted, up-to-date verification of Indigenous Enterprises against the IPP eligibility criteria.
tenders.deliverables_summary: Provide a national, independent Indigenous business verification service and associated functions: maintain accurate, current and trusted information on Indigenous Enterprises assessed against the Commonwealth's IPP eligibility criteria; support integrity, transparency and fairness in applying the strengthened IPP eligibility criteria; and work collaboratively with NIAA to help stakeholders transition from the original IPP eligibility criteria to the strengthened criteria. (Reconstructed from AusTender ATM summary via search; full scope documents were not readable this run.)
key_deliverables: National independent Indigenous business verification service
Verification of Indigenous Enterprises against strengthened IPP eligibility criteria
Maintenance of accurate, up-to-date and trusted Indigenous business information for government and public use
Support for integrity, transparency and fairness in applying the strengthened IPP eligibility criteria
Collaborative support for stakeholder transition from original to strengthened IPP eligibility criteria
tenders.questions_due: Tender-process queries to IPPTenders@niaa.gov.au; responses posted to AusTender as addenda.
tenders.briefing: Industry Briefing held Thursday 20 August 2026 at 10:30am; attendance required a completed Deed of Confidentiality and individual deed polls returned to the Contact Officer by 2pm Tuesday 18 August 2026 (AEST). Briefing window has passed.
tenders.detail_source: AusTender ATM 'Current ATM View - PROC0018432' summary and NIAA IPP reform notice, read via WebSearch snippets (detail page egress-blocked).
tenders.reasoning: Discovered on AusTender (buyer-originated Commonwealth portal) via WebSearch; corroborated by two AusTender ATM URLs (PROC0018432 and a related NOTICE) and a National Indigenous Times article on the IPP verification tender. Not present in the 477 known dedup keys.
tenders.notes: Headline + scope captured from search snippets; tender documents, evaluation criteria and value not readable this run due to egress block. Closing 18-Sep-2026 (day after this run) so still open at time of run. Buyer confirmed as NIAA via AusTender Annual Procurement Plan entry.

tenders.title: Mid-Term Review of the Climate Resilient Communities Program
tenders.buyer: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) — Australian Aid Program
tenders.category: Strategic planning / monitoring and evaluation consultancy services
tenders.description: DFAT is seeking a suitably qualified evaluation team to undertake a mid-term review of the Climate Resilient Communities Program, assessing progress and performance to inform the remainder of the program.
tenders.deliverables_summary: Design and deliver an independent mid-term review of DFAT's Climate Resilient Communities Program: assess the program's progress, effectiveness and performance against objectives and provide findings and recommendations to guide the program's remaining implementation. (Reconstructed from AusTender ATM summary via search; full terms of reference were not readable this run.)
key_deliverables: Independent mid-term review / evaluation of the Climate Resilient Communities Program
Assessment of program progress, effectiveness and performance against objectives
Findings and recommendations to inform the remainder of the program
